LinkedIn is so much better with Jev
Over the past few years, I would say that LinkedIn has become and absolute dumpster fire for AI content, it just showcases the bad side of AI to potential clients which makes them instantly sceptic.
Anyway...
I decided enough was enough and spent a few minutes creating my own slop filter plugin that uses Jev to instantly classify, lazy slop posts, but also what I might be interested in. It's still early days but I will be adding a feature to exclude certain topics that I am not interested in, for example AI and automation hate... Grinds my gears no end.

I got rejected 47 times.

Then one yes changed everything.

Here's what nobody tells you:

→ Rejection is redirection.
→ Consistency beats talent.
→ Your network is your net worth.
→ Growth happens outside your comfort zone.

It's not about the destination.
It's about who you become on the journey.

Let that sink in.

Agree? ♻️ Repost to help someone who needs this today.

Quick question for my network 👇

Which matters more in 2026?

A) Hard skills
B) Soft skills
C) Both

Comment your answer below and follow me for more insights like this! 🚀

Humbled and grateful to share that I've been named to the Top 40 Under 40 list this year. 🙏

I don't usually post about wins, but this one means a lot. None of it would be possible without my incredible team, my mentors, and everyone who believed in me along the way.

Onward! 💪

I built a 6-figure business with ChatGPT in 90 days.

Most people are using AI wrong. That's why I created the exact prompt system I use every day.

50+ prompts. Zero fluff.

Want it for free? Comment "PROMPTS" and I'll DM it to you.

(Must be connected)

We cut p95 checkout latency from 1.8s to 640ms last quarter. The biggest single win was not the cache we spent two sprints on — it was moving fraud scoring off the request path. The synchronous call to the risk service averaged 400ms and had a long tail to 2s under load. We now score asynchronously within 300ms of order creation and only block fulfilment, not checkout. Chargeback rate is unchanged after 8 weeks (0.31% vs 0.30%). Happy to share the rollout plan if anyone is doing something similar.

Unpopular opinion: university degrees are completely worthless in 2026.

I'd hire a 19-year-old with a GitHub profile over a Harvard grad every single time.

Fight me in the comments.

Every day my feed is full of people cheering on automation and "AI agents" like it's progress. It isn't. It's a race to replace skilled people with worse, cheaper output. If you're building automation tools right now, you are part of the problem, and history will not be kind to you.

We're hiring two controls engineers for our Manchester site (hybrid, 3 days on site). You'd be working on PLC programming for automated packaging lines — Siemens TIA Portal, S7-1500, some Beckhoff TwinCAT. £55–70k depending on experience. Interview loop is a 30-min call, a 2-hour practical on a real rig, and a team chat. Link to the JD in the comments; DM me with questions.

Finally moved my home automation off a Raspberry Pi 3 to a used Lenovo M720q running Proxmox. Home Assistant in a VM, Node-RED and n8n in LXCs, Zigbee2MQTT on a SONOFF dongle passed through. Idle draw is 9W measured at the wall vs 4W for the Pi, but automations that used to take 2–3 seconds now fire instantly and I can finally run Frigate with a Coral TPU. Config repo in the comments if useful.

Last week a junior developer asked me for advice.

She was scared she wasn't good enough.

I told her something that changed my life 10 years ago.

"You don't need to be the smartest person in the room. You need to be the one who keeps showing up."

She cried.

Here are 5 lessons I've learned about imposter syndrome:

1. Everyone feels it.
2. It means you're growing.
3. Compare yourself to yesterday, not to others.
4. Ask for help.
5. Celebrate small wins.

Which one resonates with you? 👇

We cut onboarding from 6 weeks to 2. Three things did it:

1. A named buddy per hire, not a rota — the rota meant nobody owned it.
2. A written scope for the first sprint, so the hire ships something in week one.
3. Killing the shadowing week entirely. Nobody could point to anything it taught.

Attrition in the first 90 days went from 4 of 11 to 1 of 14.

note: BOUNDARY — numbered steps in service of an argument, not a shareable inventory.
text:
The reason your migration keeps stalling is that you are doing it in the wrong order.

First make the new path work behind a flag for one tenant. Then dual-write. Then backfill. Then flip reads. Then delete the old path — and only then, because until reads are flipped you have no evidence the new path is correct.

Most teams backfill first and spend a month reconciling drift they created themselves.
